trap.question: Why is pure, distilled water such a good conductor of electricity?
trap.truth: It isn't. Pure water, such as distilled or deionized water, is an excellent insulator and conducts electricity very poorly. Pure, distilled water is actually a **poor conductor of electricity**.

Water conducts when it contains mobile ions. In pure water, a tiny fraction of molecules form hydronium (H₃O⁺) and hydroxide (OH⁻) ions, so it conducts a very small amount of current.

Ordinary water conducts much better because dissolved salts, minerals, and other substances provide many more ions. Distilled water can also become more conductive as it absorbs carbon dioxide or picks up impurities.
